newsitem.title: UK: DMG client concerned over Horlick row-paper.
newsitem.headline: DMG client concerned over Horlick row-paper.

text.p: A top client of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) voiced concern about destablisation at the firm and this may be a decisive factor in prompting it to take its business elsewhere, the Independent said on Thursday.

Geoff Henry, chief executive of the Merchant Navy Officers' Pension Fund, which has around 50 million stg ($84.1 million) invested at MGAM, was worried about the sudden suspension of MGAM pension fund head Nicola Horlick, the newspaper reported.
"What we are seeing now (with the suspension of Horlick) is a vital element being removed from the situation. That is a destabilisation," the Independent quoted Henry as saying.
Henry said the pension fund's trustees had been concerned before over the management structure at the group when the Peter Young affair emerged, the newspaper reported.

Last year fund manager Young was sacked for gross misconduct and is currently under investigation by Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) following the discovery of suspect valuations in three MGAM funds. Young has denied any involvement in criminal activity and said he is being made a scapegoat.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank, suspended 35-year-old Horlick "pending the outcome of an internal investigation which will look at a potential breach of her contract".
Banking sources said the suspension followed talks between Horlick and ABN Amro and overtures made by Horlick to members of her team at MGAM to move to the Dutch firm.
ABN Amro has denied it had any intention of poaching staff from MGAM.
Separately, Kleinwort Benson is seeking as much as 100,000 stg ($168,200) in damages from Tim Horlick, the husband of Nicola Horlick, the Times reported on Thursday.
The newspaper said Kleinwort had confirmed it was in litigation with Tim Horlick and that the legal action stemmed from his leaving Kleinwort last year to take up a senior post at Salomon Brothers.
"An injunction demanding that he return confidential documents and refrain from approaching former colleagues was backed by a judge in chambers and Kleinwort is now seeking damanges," the Times said.
It quoted a Kleinwort spokesman saying Tim Horlick committed a serious breach of his legal obligations as a director and that the bank was seeking a settlement.
